description: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo is an exciting night race held at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. The race offers an atmospheric experience, with headlamps illuminating the trail and reflectors along the course helping participants find their way in the dark. There are separate men’s and women’s categories across several age groups, and all participants receive a medal and the chance to win great prize-draw prizes. The event has a social atmosphere, with self-service bag storage and race-bib collection before the race.
course_highlights: The race follows trails at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann
Headlamps illuminate the course in the dark
Reflectors along the course provide visibility and safety
additional: Ledlenser will provide a limited number of headlamps for testing and borrowing during the race, on a first-come, first-served basis. There is self-service bag storage in the start area, and the baggage tag from the race bib must be attached to the bag. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for under 25, 25–39, 40–54, and over 55 years. The top three men and women overall will receive prizes. A headlamp is mandatory; a limited number of lamps can be borrowed. All participants receive a medal. Race-bib collection takes place at Löplabbet Oslo, Pilestredet 7, November 2–4, from 10:00 to 19:00, and at the start venue from 16:00 on race day. There is self-service bag storage.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 1. løp
description: Samnanger Winter Series is an inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Running Group, suitable for all ages and ability levels. The races take place at Nesodden, with a choice of 2 km or 5 km distances. The Winter Series is held roughly every other Friday throughout the winter and focuses on competition, training and socialising. The race is free and open to everyone, with an emphasis on the joy of running and community in a safe environment.
course_highlights: The race takes place at Nesodden, with the start and finish in the same place
Choose between 2 km and 5 km distances; the 5 km course has been officially measured by NFIF
The races take place in the winter darkness, so reflective vests are recommended
additional: The running group is free, open to everyone and suitable for all ability levels. Races are held roughly every other Friday at 18:30. Reflective vests are recommended because of the dark winter conditions. Samnanger IL Running Group also offers group training every Monday at 18:10 in Hagabotnane. Races are held roughly every other Friday from November to March. Remember to wear a reflective vest.

name: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Maraton
description: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Marathon 2026 is organized by Fagerstrand IF at Myklerud, Fagerstrand. This unique race starts on Saturday, November 7 at 09:00 and follows a simple but demanding format: a new 6.7 km lap starts every hour. The race continues on a “last man standing” basis until only one runner remains, or is decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing. Participants can choose their strategy: run fast for a longer break or take it easier to conserve energy. There will be a banquet for runners and their companions.
course_highlights: 6.7 km laps every hour
Last man standing format
Decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing
additional: Doors open at 08:00. There will be a banquet for runners and their +1; banquet tickets are sold separately. A service fee of NOK 15 per ticket is added at checkout (maximum NOK 30 per order). Race starts at 09:00, with doors opening at 08:00. Limited number of tickets. Banquet ticket sold separately.

name: 14. Sollingquerung
description: The Solling Crossing is a unique run from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen, taking place on November 7, 2026. The course is run exclusively by GPS, as it is not marked, making the event particularly challenging and exciting. The field is limited to 100 participants, creating a friendly atmosphere. The start is at 9:00 a.m., after runners are taken by bus from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen at 7:45 a.m. A tip for runners: anyone who completes the marathon distance at the Solling Run on June 6, 2026, is guaranteed a starting place in the Solling Crossing.
course_highlights: Course from Bad Karlshafen to Dassel
No course markings; GPS navigation only
Aid stations along the course
additional: Start at 9:00 a.m. after the 7:45 a.m. bus ride from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen. Field limited to 100 participants. No course markings; GPS navigation only. Tip: A starting place is guaranteed to participants in the Solling Run marathon on June 6, 2026. The course is unmarked, GPS navigation is required, November weather may bring rain and temperatures of around 2–7°C, no on-site entries are possible, and the event sells out quickly.

name: 6. Weserbergland Backyard Ultra
description: The Weserbergland Backyard Ultra Run is a unique ultrarunning event in Höxter, North Rhine-Westphalia, held every year in November. Participants run a lap of about 6.7 kilometers every hour until only one runner remains. The race stands out for its distinctive challenge and the camaraderie among runners. The event is known for its demanding course and the impressive performances of participants, who often run for many hours and cover many kilometers.
course_highlights: A course of approximately 6.7 km per lap
A loop course with challenging climbs on the Heiligenberg
A run through varied terrain in the Weserbergland
additional: The race traditionally starts at 10 a.m. Registration usually fills up quickly, and the field often reaches capacity early. There is currently no waiting list. The event is organized by TuS Lütmarsen e. V. Participant numbers are limited to ensure the quality and safety of the event. It is one of Germany's last major Backyard events of the year, with typical November weather and long nights. Registration opens on 1 May 2026.

name: Limes- Winterlaufserie - 1. Lauf über 10 km
description: The Limes Winter Running Series is a three-part winter running series in Pohlheim. The first race, a 10 km run, forms the basis for the overall standings. The series attracts runners from the region, particularly from the Lahn-Dill district, and has a long tradition, with its 49th edition taking place in 2026. The race offers a great opportunity to compete with other runners during the colder months and kick off the winter running series.
course_highlights: 10 km run through Pohlheim, Watzenborn-Steinberg
Part of a three-race winter running series
Popular race with regional participation, particularly from the Lahn-Dill district
additional: Typical November weather: around 7 °C, usually rainy, with an average of 45 mm of precipitation. Please check the details with the organizer before registering. Participants can look forward to a sporting challenge in a wintry atmosphere. The event is open to runners of all ability levels and also provides results and participant lists.

name: Pokallauf
description: The “Rund um Marienberg” Cup Race is a traditional running event held in the Marienberg region. Competitions are held in classic and freestyle technique, with distances of 5 km and 10 km, each run on a 2.5 km loop. The event offers runners of various age groups and ability levels a sporting challenge in a scenic setting. Due to the current snow conditions, technical and course adjustments may affect how the competition is run.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km distances on a 2.5 km loop
Classic technique for U6–U9; freestyle technique from U10
New 10 km distance from H21
additional: The event is organized by ATSV Gebirge/Gelobtland e.V. The event announcement will not be updated. Competition technique depends on age group: U6–U9 use classic technique with a mass start; U10 and older use freestyle technique with a mass start. Depending on snow conditions, the route may vary, with adjustments to technique and distance. It is a popular event for runners seeking nature and a challenge.

name: SCC Cross Country
description: The SCC Cross Country is a forest race in Berlin at the Julius-Hirsch-Sportanlage in Westend. Two clearly defined cross-country routes are offered: 4 km for U16 through adults and 9 km for U18 through adults; both races start in the morning. The event is deliberately straightforward and is aimed at club runners, young athletes and adults who want to run short off-road loops, setting it apart from the city’s major road races. The course follows paved and unpaved forest paths, where rhythm, sure footing and a fast finish matter more than scenic views. Awards go to the top three in each age and gender category, and there is a prize for the fastest final lap for men and women.
course_highlights: Forest race on paved and unpaved forest paths
Two routes: 4 km for U16 through adults, 9 km for U18 through adults
Focus on rhythm, sure footing and a fast finish
additional: Entry is free for SCC members. Late registration is available shortly before the start for an additional fee. An archive of results is available to document the race. The event takes place at the Julius-Hirsch-Sportanlage on Harbigstraße in Westend, Berlin-Charlottenburg. Typical November weather is around 7 °C, with rainy days. Forest race on paved and unpaved forest paths, entry fee for non-members, late registration for an additional fee, November weather around 7 °C, rainy.

name: Schkölener Stadtparklauf
description: The Schkölen Stadtparklauf is a long-standing running event in Schkölen, Thuringia, taking place on November 7, 2026. Organized by TSV 1885 Schkölen and SSV Friedrich-Schiller-Gymnasium Eisenberg, the event offers various distances for children, teenagers, and young adults. The routes run through the town park and include short and long loops, combined according to age group. The event emphasizes clear age-group divisions and is aimed particularly at young runners.
course_highlights: Distances from 0.6 km to 5 km, tailored to age groups
Loops through the town park, combining short and long loops
Age groups determined by calendar year for fair competitions
additional: Age groups are determined by calendar year; for example, a 6-year-old runner in 2025 belongs to age group 6. Participants are asked to enter the correct age group when registering late. Various running distances, age-group divisions, registration with the correct age, looped running on the sports field

name: Sparkassen-LüneCross
description: The Sparkassen-LüneCross is an exciting and challenging cross-country running event set amid nature and the city of Lüneburg. The varied course follows sandy, root-covered trails, meadows, forest paths and gravel tracks, testing endurance, strength and running technique. Main races are offered over 4 km and 8 km, along with shorter distances for children and young people and 8 km relay races. Alongside the sporting challenge, the focus is on the enjoyment of running and community, with a school competition and a convivial awards ceremony afterwards.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with sandy, root-covered trails
Routes through meadows, forest paths and gravel tracks
8 km relay races can be run by teams of 3 to 6 runners
additional: There is a school competition with prizes for schools with the highest participation rate. Food and refreshments are available, followed by an awards ceremony and a convivial get-together. Relay teams of 3 to 6 runners can be formed from family, colleagues, teammates or friends. The route passes through natural surroundings, including forest paths, meadows, sand and gravel. Registration is required; family and group participation is possible.

name: TSV Bayer 04 Talent- und Speed-Cross
description: The TSV Bayer 04 Talent and Speed Cross in Leverkusen is an established cross-country race, serving in particular as a talent scout event for school-age categories up to U16, as well as for the U18 and older age groups. The event is a regular fixture on the Nordrhein Cross Cup calendar and features a varied course on the grass auxiliary field at the Fritz-Jacobi-Anlage. With a tight schedule and exciting races, including cross sprints, it offers an engaging experience for both participants and spectators. The event is attracting growing numbers of participants and is accompanied by good catering and professional commentary.
course_highlights: Varied course on the grass auxiliary field at the Fritz-Jacobi-Anlage
Part of the Nordrhein Cross Cup for age groups M/W 11 to 15
Exciting cross sprints, particularly in the U18 category
additional: The event saw an increase of almost 200 participants. Good catering and professional commentary are provided. The races follow one another in a tight schedule. Dates in November 2026; cross-country race as part of the Nordrhein Cross Cup; various age groups; competition on unpaved terrain.

name: Westerwinkellauf
location: Wasserschloss Westerwinkel, Ascheberg-Herbern, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Westerwinkellauf is a traditional fun run around Westerwinkel moated castle in Ascheberg-Herbern. The course runs mainly along park paths and offers scenic surroundings. The event is open to runners and walkers of all ages and uses modern Race Result timing. The start and finish areas are at the sports and swimming hall in Herbern. Local partners provide refreshments, and professional commentary helps create a welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: Course runs mainly along park paths around Westerwinkel moated castle
Start and finish at the sports and swimming hall in Herbern
Scenic running surroundings with good facilities
additional: Timing is provided by Race Result using a disposable chip attached to the race bib, which is collected at the finish. No refunds for non-participation. Parking is available in the schoolyard of Mariengrundschule. Commentary by Janik Broszeit from Dortmund. Refreshments for participants and spectators provided by Getränke Zimmermann. Courses, start times, site map, registration, results, certificates, running and walking categories, participation for school groups, free participation for registered pupils.

name: Lauf Winterlaufserie 2026/2027
description: The 1st Winter Running Series 2026/2027 in Beverstedt-Wellen is a winter running series connected with the traditional Rund um Wellen event. It is organized by the local running club, which also runs the historic Wellen Marathon, one of the oldest marathons in Germany. The event offers a welcoming, family atmosphere, various distance options, and strong local support from volunteers, sponsors, and the local fire brigade. The organizers aim to preserve the event’s well-established challenge and familiar character.
course_highlights: Part of the long-standing Rund um Wellen event, with four distances
Rural, family-friendly atmosphere, organized by a local club
Strong local support from volunteers and the fire brigade
additional: Typical November weather: average 7 °C (minimum 2 °C) with frequent rain (45 mm of precipitation). Start location: Beverstedt-Wellen. Terrain: mixed. Registration: not specified. Further notes: Part of the Rund um Wellen event, with local support and volunteers involved.

name: 50. Hermann-Löns-Park-Lauf
location: Hermann-Löns-Park, Hannover-Wülferode, Hannover, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Hermann-Löns-Park Run in Hannover-Kirchrode is a traditional road and fun run held annually in early November. The event offers various distances from 400 m to 10 km, officially measured and approved by the German Athletics Association. It is known for its family-friendly atmosphere, volunteer support, and professional timekeeping. Runners can enjoy a raffle and refreshments in the finish area, making it a popular event in the region.
course_highlights: Officially measured 5 km and 10 km courses in accordance with German Athletics Association standards
Run through Hermann-Löns-Park in Hannover-Kirchrode
Various distances from 400 m to 10 km for all age groups
additional: Late entries are possible on site on Saturday from 14:00 to 16:00 and on Sunday from 9:00 until 45 minutes before the start. Race numbers can be collected on both days. Electronic timekeeping is used, with results recorded via race number. Spikes are not allowed and may lead to disqualification. The event takes place in all weather conditions. A €2 deposit for the race number is payable at registration. Courses from 1.5 km to 10 km, marathon relay, registration and results online

name: Braunschweiger Speed5
description: Braunschweiger Speed5 is the fastest fun run in the city of Braunschweig, organised by Polizeisportverein Braunschweig and Braunschweiger Laufclub. The running event on November 8, 2026, offers exciting races for recreational and competitive runners of all ages, including an 800 m children’s race, a 1-mile schoolchildren’s race and a measured 5 km race. The event features professional chip timing, a clear cutoff time for the fast 5 km race, and a friendly atmosphere with refreshments at the finish and music. Awards ceremonies recognise the top female and male runners in various age groups and main races.
course_highlights: Measured 5 km course with a 22-minute cutoff in the fast race
800 m children’s race and 1-mile schoolchildren’s race
Professional chip timing and awards for top finishers
additional: Race bib collection starts at 09:15 on the grounds of Polizeisportverein. Refreshments are available for runners at the finish, with musical entertainment by DJ Carlito. Paramedics will be on site for safety. A pacemaker will be available in the slower 5 km race to help runners achieve times under 20 minutes. Certificates can be accessed online or on site after the race. Course: measured 5 km, children’s and schoolchildren’s races. Registration via RaceResults. Parking is available along Georg-Westermann-Allee and Ebertallee. The event takes place in Prinzenpark.

name: Hohen Neuendorfer Herbstlauf
description: The Hohen Neuendorf Autumn Run is a traditional running event that has been held in Hohen Neuendorf since 1900 and is considered the birthplace of cross-country running in Germany. The run attracts numerous participants from the region and beyond each year and offers distances for all age groups, from a children’s run to longer distances. The event brings generations together and is supported by many volunteers and local partners. It traditionally takes place in November and is a fixture on the regional sporting calendar.
course_highlights: Traditional cross-country run with a history dating back to 1900
Participants spanning generations, from age 3 to over 90
Support from local clubs and reservists along the course
additional: The run includes various distances, including a 400-metre children’s run and a 5.5 km course. The event is supported by many volunteers, including the Roter Adler Reservists from Lehnitz. The Autumn Run is one of the largest running events in the Oberhavel district and attracts participants from various regions. It takes place at the Rudolf Harbig sports ground and is weather-dependent. Registration is via MyRacepartner. The event is known for its historical significance in cross-country running in Germany and promotes a sense of community through sport.

name: Lop dwasch dörn Wildenloh
location: Wildenloh bei Oldenburg, Landkreis Oldenburg, Niedersachsen, Germany
description: Lop dwasch dörn Wildenloh is a traditional cross-country run held in early November on the beautiful fitness trail in Wildenloh, west of Oldenburg. The name means “Run across Wildenloh” and reflects the event’s rustic character: it takes place in the forest, without showers. The event is organised by the sports club Team Laufrausch e.V., which creates a friendly, nature-oriented running atmosphere.
course_highlights: Cross-country run on the local fitness trail in Wildenloh
Rustic forest course without showers
Traditional event with regional character
additional: The run takes place on a rustic forest course without showers. Several distances are offered (short course: 1600m, middle course: 3200m), and results from previous years are available. The event is organised by the sports club Team Laufrausch e.V. The run is held annually in November. There are no showers on site, results are published, and categories include children and adults.

name: Martinslauf
location: Unterbacher See, Düsseldorf, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
organizer: SFD '75 e. V., pulsschlag, SC Grün Weiß Paderborn, Friedrich-Rister-Gedächtnislauf
description: The Martinslauf is being organized for the 48th time by SFD '75 e. V. around Unterbacher See in Düsseldorf. The event offers a variety of races for all age groups, including Bambini and youth races, an inclusion run, and Nordic walking. It is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and varied course, offering both sporting challenges and fun for the whole family. Award ceremonies for various age groups take place after the races, and participants can purchase a personalized finisher medal.
course_highlights: Loop course around Unterbacher See
A range of distances from 150 m to 10 km
Start and finish at Strandbad Süd on Unterbacher See
additional: Race packets can be mailed (for an additional fee of 4 EUR) or collected on site. Late registration is possible for a 3 EUR fee. Timing is done with a chip integrated into the race bib; there is no rental fee. Showers are available at the neighboring campsite. Free parking is available at Strandbad Süd and Strandbad Nord. A finisher medal engraved with the participant’s name and time can be ordered for 13 EUR and will be handed out on race day. The 10 km race cutoff is 13:15; the event ends at approximately 14:00. The Martinslauf combines fun runs, family events, and evening light runs, with a focus on running for fun, community, and a special atmosphere. Participation is at the participant’s own risk, with various race distances and activities for children and adults.

name: Mausebergecrosslauf
description: The Mauseberge Cross-Country Run is an autumn cross-country race held in the Mauseberge Forest near Husum in northern Germany. The course follows natural forest trails over uneven terrain, with mud and several climbs. The event is organized by the athletics department of Husumer Sportverein and is a long-standing fixture on the regional race calendar.
course_highlights: Natural forest trails in the Mauseberge Forest
Uneven, muddy terrain
Several climbs
additional: The start is in Husum, and the venue can be reached by car. Typical November weather averages 7 °C (minimum 2 °C), with frequent rain (about 45 mm of precipitation). The race takes place in November in typical autumn weather, with temperatures around 2–7 °C and rain. Registration with the organizer is recommended. Places are available for various distances, including 1 km, 3.35 km, 5 km, 6.67 km, and 8.33 km.

name: Quickborn Run über 5 km und 10 km
description: The Quickborn Run is organized by TuS Holstein Quickborn and will be held for the 47th time in 2026. There are two race distances, 5 km and 10 km, starting in Quickborn on November 8. Childcare is available for families with young children, allowing parents to take part as well. The event offers changing facilities, free parking and a free timing chip on loan. The races are open to young people aged 12 and 14 and up, respectively, and follow the rules of the German Athletics Regulations.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km race routes
Start and finish at Dietrich-Bonhoeffer-Gymnasium in Quickborn
Free timing chip on loan
additional: Start times: 10:00 a.m. for the 5 km race, 11:00 a.m. for the 10 km race. Race pack collection from 8:00 to 10:30 a.m. at Dietrich-Bonhoeffer-Gymnasium. Changing facilities in the sports hall. Free parking at the sports hall and in the AKN station parking garage. Participation from age 12 for the 5 km and age 14 for the 10 km. Registration opens on 1.7.2026 via the Race Result portal. Late registration is possible on the day of the event, but participant numbers are limited, particularly for the 5 km race. Distances: 5 km and 10 km; minimum ages: 12 for the 5 km and 14 for the 10 km; limited places; parking at the sports hall and AKN station parking garage.

name: Refrather Herbstlauf
location: Königsforst, Bergisch Gladbach-Refrath, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Refrath Autumn Run is a long-standing running classic in the Königsforst near Bergisch Gladbach-Refrath, held annually since 1986. The event offers 5 km, 10 km and half-marathon races, all measured by the DLV and eligible for the rankings. The courses run through the autumn forest and feature out-and-back routes with challenging yet scenic sections. The race attracts both competitive runners and those running for enjoyment, and concludes with prompt award ceremonies for all age groups.
course_highlights: Out-and-back routes through the autumnal Königsforst
DLV-measured courses over 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon
Scenic forest trails with challenging sections
additional: Start times: 5 km at 10:00, 10 km at 11:00, half marathon at 12:30. Award ceremonies take place promptly after runners finish. Parking is available on Rather Weg, approximately 1.2 km from the Bensberg exit of the A4. Public transport: take KVB line 1 to “Refrath”. The 5 km and 10 km courses are measured by the DLV and eligible for the rankings. Participants can register online. The courses are gently undulating, with an elevation difference of about 6 m in the 5 km race and 20 m in the 10 km race. The event has been a fixture on the region’s running calendar for many years.

name: RWW-Herbstwaldlauf
description: The RWW Herbstwaldlauf in Bottrop is a traditional race taking place on November 8, 2026. It is part of the International Marathon and Ultra Cup and offers various distances for beginners and experienced runners. The event takes place at Jahnstadion, where the Herbstwaldlauf tradition dates back to 1973. Participants can look forward to a sporting challenge amid picturesque woodland scenery, bringing together community and a passion for running.
course_highlights: Run through Bottrop’s picturesque woodland scenery
Start and finish at the historic Jahnstadion
Part of the International Marathon and Ultra Cup
additional: The time limit for all races is 15:30. A human broom wagon is available to support participants. T-shirts can be ordered in advance. The event takes place at Jahnstadion, which is also used by the Adler-Langlauf Bottrop training groups. Held in November, the race includes routes through forests and natural surroundings and offers a welcoming club atmosphere for runners of all levels.

name: Süderelbe Halbmarathon durch das Alte Land
price_range: 20 Euro Halbmarathon, 18 Euro 10 km, 5 Euro Kinderlauf
description: The 50th Süderelbe Half Marathon through the Altes Land takes place on November 8, 2026. The course starts at the CU Arena at Neugraben S-Bahn station, runs through the Altes Land to Neuenfelde, and returns to the start. In addition to the half marathon, there are 10 km and 5 km races, a 5 km walking event, and a 1.2 km children’s race. The event is organized by Hausbruch-Neugrabener Turnerschaft von 1911 e.V. and offers a varied program for runners of all ages.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the CU Arena, Neugraben S-Bahn station
Course through the scenic Altes Land to Neuenfelde
Return to the starting point along the same route
additional: The program includes 10 km and 5 km races, a 5 km walking event, and a 1.2 km children’s race. The organizer is Hausbruch-Neugrabener Turnerschaft von 1911 e.V., with office hours Mon–Fri 09:00–11:00 and Mon–Thu 16:00–18:00. The event features a course through the Altes Land, various race distances, a children’s race, a walking event, a course closing time of 12:30, parking at the P+R car park at Neugraben S-Bahn station, race-number pickup on the day of the event, refreshments along the course, and medals and certificates for participants.

name: Wernigeröder Armeleuteberglauf
description: The Wernigeröder Armeleuteberglauf is a challenging trail race in November that starts and finishes at Haus Blume in Wernigerode. The route takes runners to the Kaiserturm and offers a varied challenge, with narrow forest paths, muddy sections and steep climbs. In addition to the main races over 5.4 km and 10 km, there are also children’s races over 1 km and 2.1 km. The event is organized by Harz-Gebirgslauf 1978 e.V. Wernigerode and, with around 160 participants, is a popular local tradition that also includes a pasta party on the evening before the race.
course_highlights: Trail race on narrow forest paths
Steep climbs to the Kaiserturm
Muddy and fast downhill sections
additional: The event has four distances: 1 km and 2.1 km for children, and 5.4 km and 10 km for the main races, which start together later in the morning. A pasta party on the evening before the race is a small local tradition. Trail character with challenging climbs; registration by email; pasta party on Saturday evening at Waldgasthaus Armeleuteberg.

name: Westfalenparklauf
location: Westfalenpark Dortmund, Dortmund, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
organizer: Lauftreff Bittermark Dortmund, LT Bittermark Dortmund, Dortmunder Volksbank

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Onlineanmeldung bis 27.10.2026, 23:59 Uhr zum regulären Beitrag

description: The Dortmunder Volksbank Westfalenparklauf on 8 November 2026 is a sporting competition in Westfalenpark Dortmund, welcoming runners of all ages. The event offers various distances, including Bambini, schoolchildren’s and main races over 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km, with electronic timing. The course is measured by the DLV and runs through the beautiful Westfalenpark. All finishers receive medals, and the fastest runners are honored. The event prioritizes safe and fair race operations, with medical support and refreshments in the finish area.
course_highlights: Course in Westfalenpark Dortmund, with start and finish at the Ruhrallee entrance
DLV-measured courses over 2.5 km (1 lap), 5 km (2 laps) and 10 km (4 laps)
Electronic timing and lead bicycle for the main races
additional: Race number distribution is available on race day until 45 minutes before each start. There are no changing facilities, but baggage storage is available without liability. Headphones, dogs and strollers are not allowed. The Bambini race is untimed; participants receive a certificate only. Awards go to places 1–3 in the men’s and women’s categories for the 5 km and 10 km races, as well as to age-group winners. Medical support is available on the course and in the start/finish area. A lead bicycle accompanies the 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km races. This is a local event with a traditional character, including medals for finishers, online registration and medical support on the course. Certain participation rules apply, including a ban on dogs and umbrellas.

name: 3TuermeWEG TRAILRUN
location: Hagen Stadtwald, Hagen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The 3TürmeWEG Trailrun is a timed trail race organized by TV Hasperbach 1898 e.V. in cooperation with Hagen.Wirtschaftsentwicklung. The route runs through Hagen City Forest and follows the well-known 3TürmeWEG premium hiking trail. Along the way, runners pass three historic towers and a fallow deer enclosure and enjoy numerous views. The route has been evaluated by the International Trail Running Association (ITRA) and is part of the National League 2026. A guided course preview run with historical commentary takes place every year in August.
course_highlights: The route passes three historic towers counterclockwise: Kaiser-Friedrich-Turm, Bismarckturm, Eugen-Richter-Turm
Runs through Hagen City Forest, with a fallow deer enclosure and numerous viewpoints
Evaluated by ITRA and part of the National League 2026
additional: Limited-edition 3TT short-sleeved and long-sleeved technical shirts, as well as padded 3TT Skyrunner running socks, can optionally be ordered by 30.09.2026. A guided course preview run with historical commentary takes place on the third Thursday of every August. The route is available as a GPX file for running independently. The event offers a varied route with cultural sights, optional merchandise available to pre-order, and starts on 8 November 2026. Registration opens on 1 July 2026.

Relay race (3 x 3.5 km)
Main race (10 km)

name: Marceliński Bieg Jesienny 2026
description: Marceliński Autumn Run 2026 is a cross-country race organized in Poznań by running enthusiasts from the Biegi.Wlkp. group. The event takes place on scenic courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal. Since 2014, the organizers have focused on promoting cross-country running in Wielkopolska, offering participants a unique running experience in beautiful natural surroundings.

Courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal
Organized by experienced running enthusiasts from Wielkopolska
additional: The race route is available on Garmin Connect. Race packs can be collected using an authorization form template. Cross-country race, event in Marceliński Forest, November 8, 2026, puzzle-piece medals, forest routes

name: NightRun Rijssen
description: NightRun Rijssen takes place on Thursday, 5 November 2026, offering a unique evening experience as participants run through the centre of Rijssen, past beautiful buildings and businesses. This is not a race; it’s all about fun and the experience, with a magical atmosphere created by the lighting and evening setting. There are several distances: a 1 km kids’ run, a 5 km walking or running route, and a 10 km route for the more ambitious. The start and finish are in the centre of Rijssen, with a rolling start to keep participants moving smoothly.
course_highlights: Run through the centre of Rijssen during late-night shopping
The route goes right through buildings and businesses
Magical, festive atmosphere with lighting and evening decorations
additional: Start and finish in the centre of Rijssen at 'T Schild (next to Pearle). Rolling start in small groups to keep participants moving smoothly. The finish is at Lucky, Morsweg 8. No timing, and it is not a race. There is an opportunity to warm up at NightRun Borne on 9 October. The event takes place during late-night shopping in Rijssen city centre; it is not a race and is focused on fun and the experience. Participants light up the streets and enjoy a festive atmosphere.

name: Batavia Night Run
description: The Batavia Night Run is an atmospheric running race taking place on Friday evening, 6 November 2026, in the illuminated Batavia Quarter in Lelystad. Participants can choose from several distances, including 5 km, 10 km, 15 km, and kids’ runs of 800 and 1,500 metres. The course runs through the historic, atmospherically lit area around Museum Batavialand, creating a unique nighttime running experience. The organisers also support the charity Stichting ALS Nederland.
course_highlights: Course through the atmospherically illuminated Batavia Quarter
Distances of 5 km, 10 km, and 15 km
Kids’ runs of 800 and 1,500 metres
additional: Registration includes entry to the atmospheric night run. A Batavia Night Run shirt and cancellation insurance can be ordered as extras. The organisers work with photographers and videographers to produce promotional images. Participants must comply with the applicable traffic regulations and RIVM guidelines. Night run with registration available; charities involved; the event combines sport and entertainment in an atmospheric setting.

name: 28e Nacht van OLAT / Kennedy Trail
description: The 28th Nacht van OLAT/Kennedy-Trail takes place from Friday evening, 6 November, to Saturday, 7 November 2026, in Oirschot, the Netherlands. Participants can choose from three distances: 110 km, 80 km and 55 km, with start times in the evening and at night. The route combines paved and unpaved paths, with extensive aid stations and a pasta meal for the 110 km and 80 km runners after the night stage. All participants must finish by 19:00 on Saturday. They receive a certificate, and a medal is available for an additional fee.
course_highlights: A partly paved, partly unpaved route, with longer unpaved sections during the day
Extensive aid stations with food and drinks
Pasta meal for 110 km and 80 km participants after the night loop
additional: Start times: 110 km at 20:00; 80 km and 55 km at 23:00. Registration is approximately one hour before the start. Dogs are not allowed. All participants must finish before 19:00 on Saturday. A medal is optional for an additional fee. Night trail race with multiple distances and support; registration approximately one hour before the start; finish before 19:00 on 7 November 2026; medal available for a fee.

name: De Najaarsloop van Cialfo
description: The AV Cialfo Autumn Run is a running event held in Epe and organized by AV Cialfo. The run takes place on Wachtelenbergweg and offers participants a great opportunity to be active in the autumn in a sporty and welcoming atmosphere. Pre-registration is available until the end of October, with on-the-day registration open until 30 minutes before the start. The event attracts runners from the region and is part of the local sporting calendar.
course_highlights: Location on Wachtelenbergweg in Epe
Autumn running event
On-the-day registration available until 30 minutes before the start
additional: Pre-registration is open through 27 October via inschrijven.nl. On-the-day registration is available until 30 minutes before the start of the run. Run at Wachtelenbergweg, Epe; date has already passed; registration via online platform.

description: The Dorps Run Renswoude takes place on Saturday, 7 November 2026, and offers a suitable distance for every runner, from beginners to experienced athletes and young runners. Participants can run individually or register as a team for the corporate competition. The event is known for its friendly, sporty atmosphere in the village of Renswoude, with routes through the surrounding area. Previous editions sold out quickly, so early registration is recommended.
course_highlights: 21 km half marathon, consisting of two laps of the 10.5 km route
10.5 km route through the village and surrounding area
1 km Kids Run for young runners
additional: Race numbers can be collected on the day from 11:30 until half an hour before the start. A timing chip is attached to the back of each race number. All participants receive a medal after the event. Showers and changing rooms are available at De Hokhorst sports hall. Event photos will be posted on the website a few days afterwards, without names and with respect for privacy. Parking is available near De Hokhorst, a short walk away. The nearest train station is Veenendaal/De Klomp, with bus connections to Renswoude. Online advance registration is open until 5 November 2026; Kids Run registration is also possible on the day. Start times: half marathon at 13:45, 10 km at 14:00, Kids Run at 12:30.

description: The Duifpolder training run is a small-scale running race through the beautiful Duifpolder between Schipluiden and Maasland. Organised in spring and autumn by De Hardloper Schipluiden, the event offers three distances: 3.5 km, 7 km and 11.7 km. The race starts at 14:00 at the Trambrug in Schipluiden, close to the registration and changing venue. It’s an accessible event and ideal for training, with a friendly atmosphere and the opportunity to chat afterwards in the IJsclub Vlietland clubhouse.
course_highlights: Small-scale race through the Duifpolder between Schipluiden and Maasland
Three distances to choose from: 3.5 km, 7 km and 11.7 km
Start at the Trambrug, close to the registration venue and clubhouse
additional: Registration takes place at the IJsclub Vlietland clubhouse, Zouteveenseweg 2a, Schipluiden. Registration opens at 12:45. Changing facilities and toilets are available, but there are no showers. Drinks are available in the clubhouse after the race. Start location: Trambrug, Schipluiden; no shower facilities; drinks available after the race

name: Plantsoenloop
description: The Plantsoenloop Groningen is Groningen’s oldest and most beautiful running race, suitable for young and old, with four different distances. This atmospheric event takes place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, and takes participants along a beautiful hilly course through Noorderplantsoen. This 68th edition is a true running classic that should not be missed in your calendar.
course_highlights: Beautiful hilly course
Run through Noorderplantsoen
Four different distances for all ages
additional: Four different distances, course through Noorderplantsoen, organised from Sportcentrum Kardinge

name: Salbam Lemelerbergloop
description: The Salbam Lemelerbergloop is a challenging cross-country race held on the Lemelerberg near Ommen. The race is part of the Vechtdal Cross Competitie and offers several distances: a 2 km youth race and approximately 6 km and 12 km races for adults. The course is entirely off-road and hilly, with significant elevation changes in the Lemelerberg nature reserve, the largest nature reserve managed by Landschap Overijssel. The race is ideal for runners who enjoy a challenging trail run in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Entirely off-road course
Hilly terrain with significant elevation changes
Lemelerberg nature reserve near Ommen
additional: Start times: 2 km youth race at 12:30, 6 km at 13:00, 12 km at 14:00. The race is part of the Prins Sport Vechtdal Cross Competitie, which consists of five races in total. To be eligible for the overall win, participants must take part in and finish four of the five races. Several distances, start times for youth and adults, and part of a regional cross-country competition.

name: Schipholloop
location: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Haarlemmermeer, North Holland, Netherlands
description: The Schipholloop returns on 7 November 2026 as a unique running event around Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. With a rich history spanning more than 50 years, this 60-kilometre ultrarun offers a pure, partially self-supported trail experience focused on the experience and the challenge. Participants can choose from several distances, including a half marathon and the ultrarun, and enjoy a beautiful route through the varied polder landscape, with breathtaking views. With a limited field of no more than 100 participants, it is an exclusive and unforgettable run for long-distance runners of all levels.
course_highlights: An iconic 60 km ultrarun around the Haarlemmermeerpolder
Beautiful, varied surroundings with unexpected and breathtaking views
Trail-style run with GPS navigation and full autonomy
additional: A maximum of 100 participants per edition. Not a traditional race with tape and traffic marshals. The run is partially self-supported and trail-style, with GPS navigation and fixed checkpoints. A special tryout edition was held on 23 May ahead of the November edition. Limited to 100 participants, with facilities such as drop bags, aid stations with drinks and snacks, and medals for finishers. The event emphasises the experience and natural surroundings, and is organised as a private initiative and by AV Haarlemmermeer.

name: Waalbosrun
location: Bezoekerscentrum De IJsvogel, Rijsoord, South Holland, Netherlands
description: The Waalbosrun is a fun and sporty running event organised by IJsclub Rijsoord in collaboration with De IJsvogel visitor centre. Participants follow a beautiful route through the Waalbos in Rijsoord, along green paths, waterways and wooded areas. The event is suitable for both beginner and experienced runners, with different distances for all ages. The start and finish are at the visitor centre, where supporters are welcome to cheer on the runners. Alongside sport, the event celebrates a friendly atmosphere and community spirit, and part of the proceeds go to charity.
course_highlights: A beautiful route through the Waalbos along green paths
Run alongside waterways and through wooded areas
Start and finish at De IJsvogel Visitor Centre
additional: There are three distances: the Kidsrun (approx. 1.8 km) starts at 12:00, the 10 km starts at 13:00, and the 5 km starts at 13:10. The start and finish are at De IJsvogel Visitor Centre. The event is suitable for all ages, and part of the proceeds go to charity. Participants contribute to a good cause; the event takes place in autumn, when cool and changeable weather is expected.

name: Zuidduinloop
location: Katwijk aan Zee, South Holland, Netherlands
description: The Zuidduinloop is part of the Duinloopcircuit, a unique running series along the most beautiful coastal areas of the Netherlands. The race offers a varied course with challenging dune trails and fast beach sections, suitable for both competitive runners and recreational runners. The atmosphere is always fantastic, and the event invites everyone to enjoy running outdoors. The Zuidduinloop takes place in Katwijk aan Zee and is part of a series of running events held throughout the year.
course_highlights: Varied course with dune trails and beach sections
Unique coastal setting in Katwijk aan Zee
Suitable for a range of ages and abilities
additional: There are rankings for all distances, separated into girls/women and boys/men, based on the four best results in the circuit. Race in Katwijk aan Zee, with various distances including short kids’ runs and longer races, plus GPX routes and results.

name: Knallende Kilometer
location: Familierestaurant Bergsche Plas, Bergschenhoek, South Holland, Netherlands

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Kosten € 7,50 om deel te nemen inclusief een pannenkoek OF kop snert van Familierestaurant Bergsche Plas.

description: De Knallende Kilometer is a unique running event organized by Athletics and Walking Club De Kieviten, taking place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at Familierestaurant Bergsche Plas in Bergschenhoek. It is a time-trial start, with each runner setting off individually at 30-second intervals, giving you the chance to run a fast kilometer on a straight, flat course. Afterward, instead of a medal, you’ll receive a delicious pancake or a warm bowl of snert as a reward. The event is open to both competitive runners and recreational runners looking to enjoy a friendly run.
course_highlights: Straight, flat 1,000-meter course on the cycle path above the Rottemerentunnel
Start near the 'Zwijnenplaats' car park and finish near the 'Mollenplaats' car park
Individual time-trial start from 11:00, with a new runner setting off every 30 seconds
additional: Collect your race number at Familierestaurant Bergsche Plas. The best place to park is Mollenplaats. After finishing, you’ll receive a pancake or a bowl of snert at the restaurant. Participants will receive their start time by email one week before the event. On-the-day registration is not possible, and places are limited. Flat, 1,000-meter course on the cycle path above the Rottemerentunnel; start at Familierestaurant Bergsche Plas; parking at Mollenplaats; advance registration required.

name: Athlos Hydro Trail Run
description: The Athlos Hydro Trail Run takes place on Saturday, November 7, in Harderwijk, Veluwe. This trail run offers a challenging route through the beautiful natural surroundings of the Veluwe, where participants can enjoy autumn scenery and water crossings. The event is organized by Atletiekvereniging Athlos, known for its involvement in the local running community. The Hydro Trail Run is a sporting and recreational event for trail runners who enjoy a varied course.
course_highlights: Trail run through the natural surroundings of the Veluwe
Beautiful autumn scenery
Water crossings and challenging terrain
additional: Photos from the 2025 edition are available in various albums. The start and finish of the routes are in the center of Harderwijk. The organizers use mobile photographers to capture water fun and other moments. Trail run over varied terrain, including forest, heathland, and sand; registration open; collaboration with sponsors; practical information and results available.

name: Slangenburg trailrun
description: The Slangenburg Trailrun takes place on Saturday, 7 November 2026, at De Pokkershutte in IJzevoorde. This trail run takes you along winding forest paths and unpaved routes, surrounded by the beautiful autumn colours of the Slangenburg forest. There are four distances to choose from, including a special Kidsrun for young trail runners aged 6 and up, and an official half marathon of 21.1 kilometres. The atmosphere is relaxed, with the focus on enjoying nature and exercising outdoors, without an awards ceremony.
course_highlights: Winding forest paths and unpaved routes
Autumn colours in the Slangenburg forest
Official half marathon route of over 21 kilometres
additional: There are aid stations along the way with drinks and snacks. First aid is available during the trail run. description: The Olympisch Stadionloop 2026 takes place on November 8 at the iconic Olympic Stadium in Amsterdam. Organized by Athletics Club Phanos in collaboration with Run2Day, this running event includes an 800-meter race for children and 5- and 10-kilometer races for individuals, school groups, and corporate teams. The routes pass through the Olympic Stadium and Amsterdamse Bos, and the race is part of Rondje Mokum 2026. The Olympisch Stadionloop combines sport with a good cause, as participants run in support of UNICEF.

Participants in the 5 km and 10 km races can start in designated start pens. Race numbers are distributed before the race. Medals and water are available after the finish. AV Phanos may use photos and video footage for communications. Registration is via online forms; changing rooms and showers are available for teams. The event is part of a series of local runs and takes place in and around the Olympic Stadium in Amsterdam.

name: LoveLife Run Deventer
description: LoveLife Run Deventer is a special running event taking place on 8 November 2026, where (former) cancer patients take part alongside their loved ones and healthcare providers. Participants can choose to walk or run 1 or 5 kilometres, aiming to reach the finish at their own pace, with no timekeeping. Special training sessions led by experienced running coaches from AV Daventria 1906 are offered to help participants prepare. Proceeds from the event go towards groundbreaking cancer research and local causes at Deventer Hospital, Kenniscentrum Oncologie and IPSO centrum Salland. Everyone is welcome to take part, including people who have not had cancer themselves.
course_highlights: 1- and 5-kilometre routes around Deventer Hospital and the Brinkgreven grounds
Wheelchair-accessible routes for both 1 km and 5 km
Start and finish at Radiotherapie Groep, next to Deventer Hospital
additional: Participants receive a mandatory LLR shirt, which is handed out on the day. There is no timekeeping; the aim is to reach the finish. There are 12 weeks of guided training for (former) cancer patients, led by AV Daventria 1906, starting on 19 August 2026. The event is organised by a local team of volunteers and supported by running coaches. Participants are advised to travel sustainably by bike or public transport. Participation is at your own risk. Participants are encouraged to use sustainable transport and wear an LLR shirt supplied by the organisers. The event is free for participants and focuses on fundraising for cancer research and local causes.

The route passes through the wooded estate of 't Reelaer and the undulating terrain of Raalterwoold, with approximately 90% unpaved paths. The course features woodland sections, avenues, meadows with elevation changes, and sometimes muddy stretches, making for a varied and demanding running experience. There are short youth races and more demanding 5 and 10 kilometre distances, and the race is part of the Sallands Cross Circuit.
course_highlights: Approximately 90% unpaved paths
Routes through the estate of 't Reelaer and Raalterwoold
Woodland sections, avenues, meadows with elevation changes, and muddy stretches
additional: The race is part of the Sallands Cross Circuit. Construction work is visible around the Hoftheater, offering an extra glimpse of the surroundings. Results and course records are kept, and previous results are available through the race administration. The race offers various distances, including 5 and 10 km, as well as short youth races. The course is characterised by natural, often muddy paths and varied scenery.

A spooky, eerie atmosphere, with ominous characters along the route
Start at the Markt, near Matteucci ice cream parlour
additional: Individuals may participate from age 16; younger participants may join only when accompanied by a parent or adult. Start time is between 19:00 and 20:00. The walk is not a race, but an event with a spooky atmosphere. Registration for the Krollenloop itself is sold out, but registration for the Halloween City Walk is still open. Start at 19:00; registration via the website. Participants aged 16 and over may take part independently; younger participants must be accompanied by an adult.

name: Boerenkoolloop
location: Atletiekbaan van AV NOVA, Warmenhuizen, Noord-Holland, Netherlands

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Schrijf je vòòr 1 oktober in tegen de prijzen van 2025: 10km wedstrijd/trim/bedrijvenloop: EUR 14.00

tiers.label: tier_2

description: The Boerenkoolloop in Warmenhuizen is a friendly race and fun run over 5 and 10 km, starting and finishing on the AV NOVA athletics track. The course passes through the villages of Tuitjenhorn, Eenigenburg and Warmenhuizen, partly along quiet polder roads and the historic Westfriese Omringdijk, where the wind can be a challenging factor. After the event, every participant receives a bag of ingredients for a delicious boerenkool mash, sponsored by Koninklijke VEZET. There is also a 1.2 km youth run and an approximately 11 km walk, which follows a partly reversed route. The venue offers spacious changing rooms, hot showers and additional amenities for comfort.
course_highlights: Start and finish on the AV NOVA athletics track
Route along quiet polder roads and the historic Westfriese Omringdijk
Views of the surrounding landscape, with the wind as a challenging factor
additional: Race numbers are mailed out and should arrive around 30 October. They can also be collected from the Harenkarspelhal next to AV NOVA up to 15 minutes before the start. Spacious changing rooms and hot showers are available. After the event, everyone receives a boerenkool package with sausage, potatoes and herbs. Parking is available at AV NOVA and at Bejo Zaden BV, approximately 800 metres away. The walking event starts between 8:30 and 9:30; participants must reach the finish by 12:30 to receive the boerenkool package. Registration is via Inschrijven.nl until 25 October; same-day registration is not available. Start times are 11:10, 11:25 and 11:35. Start and finish are on the AV NOVA athletics track.

name: Bosloop Malden
description: The Bosloop Malden is a running race with a rich history dating back to 1978, held on Sunday, November 1, 2026. It is a popular event among the smaller running races in the Netherlands, ideal for testing your form two weeks before the Zevenheuvelenloop. The race offers 5, 10 and 15 km routes through the woods, as well as special races for young runners, including the Bambinoloop for children aged 3 to 8 and a 2 km race for children aged 9 to 12. Participation is free for children up to 12 years old, made possible in part by sponsor Medical Training Malden. Registration is open from September 1 through October 30, 2026, and closes once the maximum number of participants per distance has been reached.
course_highlights: Run through the woods of Malden
Distances of 5, 10 and 15 km
Special youth distances: Bambinoloop and 2 km Kidsrun
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 9:00 a.m. at the event grounds. The Bambinoloop has two starts: first ages 3–5, then ages 6–8. There is no timekeeping for the Bambinoloop. The 2 km race is part of the Scholenbokaal of the MTM Kidsrun Bosloop Malden. Registration on race day is not possible. Places are limited for each distance. Distances include 2 km, 5 km, 10 km and 15 km, with special races for children; participation is free for children under 12; registration runs from September 1 to October 30, 2026; registration on race day is not possible.

name: Haarlerbergloop
distance_verbose: 30 km, Halve marathon, 16 km, 10 km, 10 km, 5 km, 2.5 km, 1 km
price_range: € 2 voor herinneringsmedaille, overige kosten niet gespecificeerd
description: The Haarlerbergloop is a challenging running event in the beautiful surroundings of the Sallandse Heuvelrug, with almost entirely unpaved trails across fields, sandy tracks, woodland and heathland. The event takes place over two days: the Haarlerbergtrail, with distances of 11, 16, 22 and 30 km, is on Saturday 31 October 2026, while the shorter distances of 1, 2.5, 5 and 10 km take place on Sunday 1 November 2026. The event is small-scale and is part of the Sallands Cross Circuit and the CrossCircuit van het Oosten. The start and finish are on Molenweg in Haarle, near café De Droadnagel, where facilities including toilets and a changing area are available.
course_highlights: Almost entirely unpaved trails across fields, sandy tracks, woodland and heathland
Beautiful routes through Sallandse Heuvelrug National Park
Steep hills and wide-open views
additional: The start and finish are on Molenweg in Haarle, near café De Droadnagel, with toilets and a changing area but no showers. Collecting your race number and leaving your bag are at your own risk. On-the-day registration is not available; advance registration is open until 30 minutes before the start. Participants in the 5 and 10 km races can buy a commemorative medal after the race (€ 2). The trail is limited to 349 participants, and registration closes no later than 31 October at 11:30, or earlier if full. Bringing your own drinking cup is mandatory for the trail; a reusable cup is available to buy (€ 4). There is no prize-giving for the trail, but every participant receives a medal. The 5 and 10 km races donate € 1 per participant to Stichting Support for Nature. Distances: 1 km, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km, 11 km, 16 km, 22 km and 30 km; cross-country event; registration opens in September; contribution to Support for Nature; races include the trail and youth distances.

name: Loop Esch Door
description: Loop Esch Door is a running event in and around the centre of Tubbergen, featuring a challenging, fast course across the Tubbergse Esch. Since 2022, the event has grown into an established race with a welcoming atmosphere and a great mix of competition and recreation. It offers various distances for runners of all levels, including special runs for children and people with disabilities. The start and finish are at Raadhuisplein in Tubbergen, where a friendly, community spirit is also central.
course_highlights: Fast course through the countryside and across the Tubbergse Esch
Start and finish at Raadhuisplein in the centre of Tubbergen
Various distances from 500 metres to 10 kilometres, including walking routes
additional: Collect race numbers on 1 November from 08:00 at Tubbergen Town Hall, up to 30 minutes before the start. Walkers can collect their race numbers from 09:00. Parking at the swimming pool on Sportlaan is recommended. There is a water station on the course, and sports nutrition is available after the event. First aid is available along the course. KinderKroon KidsRuns start from 12:45, with different age categories. Prize-giving ceremonies take place shortly after each distance finishes. The event also offers an inclusive run for people with disabilities and has a friendly, community-focused atmosphere.

name: Maasduinenloop
location: Afferden, Nationaal Park De Maasduinen, Limburg, Netherlands

description: The Maasduinenloop is an atmospheric running event held in De Maasduinen National Park, starting and finishing at Golfbaan Bleijenbeek in Afferden. The run offers a unique experience amid beautiful natural surroundings and combines sport with a friendly atmosphere. All proceeds go to burn care at the Expertise Centre for Child Trauma and Burn Care at Radboudumc Amalia Children’s Hospital. The Maasduinenloop welcomes runners of all ages and abilities, with a special focus on young participants through the Kidsrun.
course_highlights: Run through De Maasduinen National Park
Start and finish at atmospheric Golfbaan Bleijenbeek
New routes, including a 10 km loop
additional: Kidsrun start times: 10:30 (up to and including age 7, 500 m) and 10:45 (ages 8 to 11, 1,000 m). All Kidsrun participants receive a medal and a healthy snack. The prize ceremony takes place immediately after the Kidsrun, at approximately 11:00. Teams may be all-male, all-female or mixed; the score is the combined time of the three fastest runners. Team members are automatically entered in the individual race at no extra cost. Start and finish at Golfbaan Bleijenbeek. Distances range from 500 metres to 10 km. The course is marked and supervised by traffic marshals and mountain bikers, and timing is provided. Start and finish at Landgoed Bleijenbeek.

description: The Warnsborncross is a traditional cross-country race held on the beautiful Warnsborn estate near Arnhem. The race follows unpaved paths past streams and ponds, with challenging elevation changes. There are three distances: 5.5 km, 11 km and 16.5 km, covering 1, 2 or 3 laps of 5.5 km respectively. There is also a 1,200-metre Kidsrun for children up to and including 12 years old. The start and race-number pickup take place at Tennisvereniging Schaarsbergen.
course_highlights: Unpaved paths through the Warnsborn estate
Running alongside streams and ponds
Challenging elevation changes
additional: Race-number pickup is available from 9:30 until 10:45 at the latest at Tennisvereniging Schaarsbergen, Kemperbergerweg 671a, 6816 RT Arnhem. The Kidsrun starts at 10:30, and the other distances start at 11:00. Start and registration at Tennisvereniging Schaarsbergen; the course follows unpaved paths with elevation changes and is suitable for both recreational and competitive runners.

name: Zorg en Zekerheid Circuit
description: The Zorg en Zekerheid Circuit starts on 1 November 2026 and consists of nine varied running events spread over six months in the Groene Hart. The circuit is suitable for both beginner and experienced runners and offers a platform where taking part matters more than winning. Participants can choose from different distances and benefit from a discounted circuit entry, including a free running shirt and a finisher’s gift for taking part in 8 or 9 events. The circuit encourages participation and promises a friendly, sporting atmosphere.
course_highlights: Nine varied runs in the Groene Hart
Distances of 5 km, 10 km, 10 English miles and half marathon
Route along the picturesque Kromme Mijdrecht river and through Wickelhofpark
additional: Circuit participants can switch between the short and middle distances as often as they like at the information desk. Switching to the long distance is not possible without a separate entry. There is a 10 km walk, a Family Run and a G-Run for children up to 12 years old. Lost race numbers can be replaced at the information desk. Changing rooms and showers are available, as is limited bag storage. Coffee, tea and soft drinks are available for collection in the sports hall. The prize-giving takes place in the sports hall. Nine varied runs between November 2026 and April 2027, including short, middle and long distances and a half marathon, with extra rewards for taking part in multiple events.

name: LPR - Last Pirate Running
description: LPR - Last Pirate Running is a running event taking place in Volendam on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The race offers a short distance of 1.6 kilometers, ideal for a fast and challenging running experience. Registration closes on October 20, 2026, and participants can sign up via the specified registration website. The event is organized by ProRun and is suitable for runners looking for a unique and accessible race.
course_highlights: Short distance of 1.6 km
Organized in picturesque Volendam
Fast and challenging course
additional: Registration for the 1.6 km distance closes on October 20, 2026. A training plan for 10 English miles (16.1 km) is available on the website and may help with preparation. Registration for the race was closed as of October 2026; the event is intended for runners who want to enjoy a short and fun race in North Holland.

name: Kievit Sport Twentsche Cross Competitie
organizer: AV Goor, AV Iphitos, ASV Eibergen, AAV Sisu, AC Tion, LAAC Twente
description: The Kievit Sport Twentse Cross Competition is a challenging cross-country series comprising six races in Twente’s beautiful natural areas. The competition offers a unique opportunity to test yourself against peers and enjoy the region’s winter conditions. The races vary in distance and are open to different age categories, from youth to masters. With strong local involvement and sponsors such as Kievit Sport and Wiggers Vleeswaren, this competition is a much-loved event among runners in Twente.
course_highlights: Natural cross-country courses in various natural areas of Twente
Distances range from 1 km for youth to 10 km for seniors and masters
A unique collaboration between six athletics clubs in the region
additional: Race numbers can be collected at locations such as Zwembad de Vijf Heuvels (Markelo). Changing rooms and toilets are available. For age categories, the reference date is the participant’s age at the final race for youth and at the first race for masters. The competition is made possible in part by local sponsors and six athletics clubs. A 2.5/5 km Canicross distance is also held during the Hulsbeekcross. The competition includes races such as Hessenheemcross, Wintercross, Oudejaarscross, Rutbeekcross, Hulsbeekcross and Dinkelcross, with results and standings available on the official website.

description: The Maple Leaf Wintercup 2026, held on Sunday, November 1 at Bosbad De Vuursche in Baarn, is an atmospheric running and walking event set against a beautiful autumn backdrop. The race is organized by Gooise Atletiek Club Hilversum and Baarnse Atletiek Vereniging and offers challenging unpaved courses surrounded by autumn colors. There are various distances for both walkers and runners, including youth distances and recreational runs with and without a competition licence. The start and finish are on the atmospheric grounds around Bosbad De Vuursche, creating a fun and sporty atmosphere for all participants.
course_highlights: Challenging unpaved course amid autumn colors
Long Cross of 9.5 km with 4 laps
Short Cross of 3.1 km with 2 laps
additional: Race numbers can be collected from October 25 through 31 at Run2Day Hilversum or on race day at race headquarters. There is no separate gender categorization for the Short and Long Cross. Pupils of the organizing athletics clubs can participate free of charge after registering via the contact form. There is a recreational run and a competition-licence run for the short and long cross. The courses consist of multiple laps depending on the distance. The course includes unpaved paths, with events such as Nordic walking, cross-country running and youth races; start and finish at Bosbad De Vuursche.

name: Spaarnwoudecross
description: The Mokums Cross Circuit is a series of four woodland cross-country races in the Amsterdam area, including the Spaarnwoude Cross, organized by Haarlem Atletiek in Spaarndam. Participants register for at least three of these races and have a chance to receive a fun memento. There is a standings competition for the main events, with each runner’s best three results from the four races counting. The circuit is made possible through a partnership between five Amsterdam athletics clubs and their sponsor.
course_highlights: Woodland cross-country races in the Amsterdam area
Four different locations: Spaarndam, Amsterdamse Bos, De Eenhoorn, Gaasperplas
A memento for participants in at least three races
additional: Participants in at least three races receive a memento. The 20 fastest men and women in the main events score points toward the overall standings. The prize-giving takes place at the first race of the season. A muddy cross-country race and family and youth event, held on 2 November 2025 in Haarlem at Wheelerplanet in Spaarndam, with participants such as Tessa Weening and Sophie Kwak.

name: Van de Meerendonk Heidetrail
location: Gilde Sint Sebastiaan, Oirschot, North Brabant, Netherlands
description: The Van de Meerendonk Heath Trail is a beautiful recreational event across the expansive Oirschot heathland, suitable for runners and walkers. The routes are clearly marked with arrows, making it impossible to get lost. Water and fruit stations are available on all distances, and afterwards you can enjoy a friendly atmosphere with free coffee or tea and a treat. The event starts at Gilde Sint Sebastiaan in Oirschot, with several distances available for both running and walking.
course_highlights: Expansive woodland and heathland
Routes clearly marked with arrows
Water and fruit stations on all distances
additional: Start location: Gilde Sint Sebastiaan, Wintelresedijk 1, 5688GW Oirschot. Runners start between 8:30 and 9:30, walkers between 9:00 and 9:30. Toilet and changing facilities are limited; there are no showers. Free coffee or tea and a treat are available after the event until 13:00. Members of Atletiek Oirschot pay €5,00 for all distances when registering in advance. Registration and payment on the day are possible but discouraged. Routes are marked with arrows; water and fruit stations are available on all distances. Start time is between 8.30 and 9.30. There are no prizes. Free coffee and tea are provided after the event. Participation is at your own risk. Facilities are limited, with no showers.

name: Leesten Cross
description: The Leestencross is a recreational cross-country race held in the beautiful woodland around Ugchelen. The race offers a challenging course along forest, sand and heathland paths, with no muddy sections, and rewards you with a magnificent view over the heath. It’s an ideal opportunity to test your fitness and race performance in a welcoming and accessible setting. The start and finish are at Bospaviljoen ’t Leesten, a top destination for runners in the Netherlands.
course_highlights: Course along forest, sand and heathland paths
Magnificent view over the heath
Start and finish at Bospaviljoen ’t Leesten in Ugchelen
additional: After handing in your race number, you will receive a voucher for a refreshment. No changing facilities are available. First aid is available. The 10 km race counts toward AV Veluwe’s cross-country club championship. Trail run on sand paths in Kroondomein, approximately 60 metres of elevation gain, registration closed, start/finish location: Wildrooster Wenum-Wiesel, no showers or changing facilities, first aid available.

name: Twentse Smokkel Trail
description: The Twentse Smokkel Trail is a unique trail run in the border region of Losser, taking place on 1 November 2026. The routes are 90% unpaved and cross varied terrain with many singletracks, taking participants to places where running is normally not allowed. There are several distances, from challenging 27 km and 22 km runs to a 10 km Drop Off Trail, where participants are taken to the start by horse and covered wagon. In addition to the trail runs, there is a walking trail and a kids’ trail. Participants symbolically smuggle a packet of butter across the border and receive a Twentse krentenwegge after the finish as a reward.
course_highlights: 90% unpaved paths with many singletracks
The route passes through unspoilt forests and nature ponds, and along the Dinkel
A unique border crossing with symbolic butter smuggling and musical support along the way
additional: Refreshment stations are located at approximately 11 km and 4 km before the finish, plus a water station 2 km before the finish. The start and finish are at the Multifunctionele Accommodatie, Nilantspad 3 in Losser, where changing rooms, showers and toilets are available. The 10 km Drop Off Trail starts at the German monastery in Bardel; participants are taken to the start by horse and covered wagon. Timing is provided for the 27, 22 and 14 km trails, but not for the 10 km Drop Off Trail. Dogs are not allowed. After the finish, participants receive a wooden medal and a Twentse krentenwegge. The three fastest men and women in each distance are presented with a handmade smuggling trophy. Trail and walking routes on unpaved paths, including a kids’ trail and a drop-off trail, with a theme of smuggling history and experiencing nature. Registration opens on 1 July 2026 via inschrijven.nl, with participant limits for each distance and refreshment stations at 11 and 23 km.
